core_obligations: Assume the contrary: for every monic polynomial P the operator P(T) is invertible (proof line 7099).
Use that assumption to make V a vector space over the rational function field k(t) by letting polynomials in t act through T (proof lines 7099-7100).

Compare cardinalities: the dimension of k(t) over k is at least the cardinality of k, for instance since the elements 1/(t - lambda) are k-linearly independent, which contradicts the assumed bound on the dimension of V (proof lines 7100-7102).
proof_roadmap: Argue by contradiction and manufacture a k(t)-vector space structure on V from invertibility of all polynomial expressions in T (proof lines 7098-7100).
Bound the dimension of k(t) over k from below by the cardinality of k and contradict the hypothesis (proof lines 7100-7103).
difficulty_reason: For a nonzero vector space V over a field k whose dimension as a cardinal is smaller than the cardinality of k, the lemma produces, for any linear operator T, a monic polynomial P with P(T) not invertible (statement lines 7089-7096). The proof is a contradiction from the opposite assumption: if every monic polynomial in T were invertible then V would carry a k(t)-vector space structure, whose dimension over k is at least the cardinality of k because the elements 1/(t - lambda) are k-linearly independent, contradicting the bound on the dimension of V (proof lines 7098-7103). The cardinal comparison rather than an algebraic computation is what settles the statement. H2.
